name: Certificate Chain Parser
description: Sort scattered certificates into the correct leaf → intermediate → root order and report whether the root is missing.

examples.label: Sort a leaf → intermediate → root chain

hints.order: Ordering matches AKID ↔ SKID first and falls back to the subject / issuer text; when several candidates sit at the same level the first in input order wins.
hints.ambiguous: "Input already ordered" being false only means the input had to be reordered — it is not a failure.
hints.limit: A chain may hold up to 64 certificates.

faq.q: In which order should a chain be?
faq.a: Leaf certificate → intermediate CA → root CA.
The last certificate in the chain is not self-signed, which means the root was not included.

faq.q: Does the tool download missing certificates?
faq.a: No, it is purely local; use the certificate chain fetcher for downloads.
